'''Karina Morgenstern''' (born 12 February 1968 in [[Bonn]]) is a German [[physicist]]. She is a professor of [[physical chemistry]] at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref name="a">{{cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Karina Morgenstern |url=https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/pc1/lehrstuhl/cv-morgenstern.html.en |website=www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de |access-date=23 July 2020}}</ref>

== Education ==

She studied physics and computer science at the universities of [[University of Bonn|Bonn]] and [[University of Knoxville|Knoxville]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Karina Morgenstern |url=https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/pc1/lehrstuhl/cv-morgenstern.html.en |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de}}</ref> She was awarded a diploma in physics in 1993 ([[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] and [[University of Bonn]]), and a diploma in computer science in 1994 (GMD Forschungszentrum Informationstechnik and University of Bonn). She then   obtained a doctoral degree in [[surface physics]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morgenstern |first1=K. |last2=Niehus |first2=H. |last3=Comsa |first3=G. |title=Reconstruction of the oxygen covered Cu3Au(110) surface investigated by low energy ion back scattering and LEED |journal=Surface Science |date=10 September 1995 |volume=338 |issue=1 |pages=1–10 |doi=10.1016/0039-6028(95)00565-X |bibcode=1995SurSc.338....1M |language=en |issn=0039-6028}}</ref> in 1996 ([[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] and [[University of Bonn]]) and completed her [[habilitation]] in [[experimental physics]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morgenstern |first1=Karina |last2=Braun |first2=Kai-Felix |last3=Rieder |first3=Karl-Heinz |title=Surface-State Depopulation on Small Ag(111) Terraces |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=6 November 2002 |volume=89 |issue=22 |article-number=226801 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.226801 |pmid=12485090 |bibcode=2002PhRvL..89v6801M }}</ref> in 2002 ([[Free University of Berlin]]).<ref name="a"/>

== Career ==
Morgenstern  was a researcher at the [[University of Aarhus]] in 1996, then at the [[University of Lausanne]] from 1996 to 1999 and at the [[Free University of Berlin]] from 1999 to 2003. She then became a professor of [[solid state physics]] at the [[University of Hannover]] in 2005 and from 2012 she was a professor of physical chemistry at the Ruhr University Bochum.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chair of Physical Chemistry I |url=https://www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/pc1/ |website=www.ruhr-uni-bochum.de}}</ref>
Since 2018, she has been the director of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]] graduate school "Confinement-controlled Chemistry" and the dean of the department of chemistry and biochemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.confinement-controlled-chemistry.de|title=Confinement-controlled Chemistry|first=Sandra|last=Jendrzej|website=www.confinement-controlled-chemistry.de}}</ref>

== Awards and fellowships ==
* Günther Leibfried Prize 1997 of Forschungszentrums Jülich for an outstanding doctoral thesis.<ref name="a"/>
* [[Hertha Sponer Prize]] 2002 (inaugural winner) of the [[German Physical Society]] for dynamic scanning tunneling microscopy of nanostructures, which she also dealt with in her thesis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/preise/preistraeger_hs.html|title=List of laureates of the Hertha Sponer Prize|access-date=2019-04-08|archive-date=2019-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190101200852/http://www.dpg-physik.de/preise/preistraeger_hs.html}}</ref><ref>Karina Morgenstern, Dynamik von Nanostrukturen auf Ag(111): eine rastertunnelmikroskopische Untersuchung mit hoher Zeitauflösung, Dissertation Bonn 1996</ref>
* [[Heisenberg Programme|Heisenberg fellowship]] 2003–2005 of the [[German Research Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web |title=DFG - GEPRIS - Professorin Dr. Karina Morgenstern |url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/person/1701827 |website=gepris.dfg.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]] |access-date=23 July 2020}}</ref>
